capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor task (vendor + bank details + amount)

inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: The prompt assumes 'payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no independent destination verification and trusts the task's bank details outright. The safety control the prompt relies on does not exist downstream.

'Only pay vendors on the approved list' implies a safety guarantee, but as designed this is a vendor-name check, not a bank-account verification, so it does not prevent payment redirection fraud via a spoofed or compromised vendor email.
'Choose the best one' leaves vendor-quote selection criteria undefined, letting a fraudulent or compromised quote win on price or presentation alone.

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: The gate itself is a human decision independent of model capability, but it occurs before any vendor quote exists and its approval record is never passed to payments-agent, so it cannot evaluate or constrain the specific vendor or bank details actually paid.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only through the orchestrator's compliance with its own system prompt. It checks vendor name/identity, not bank account ownership, so a spoofed or compromised vendor email carrying altered bank details can still satisfy it. A more capable or manipulated model can rationalize a match between a listed vendor and a fraudulent quote.

controls.name: Structural confirmation that payment destination matches a verified record for the approved vendor
controls.decay_rationale: Would bind the payment destination to a system-of-record bank detail (e.g., pre-registered account or out-of-band callback verification) rather than to the content of an inbound quote email. This does not decay with model capability because the destination is never sourced from model output.

controls.name: Fresh raw-action approval of the specific vendor and bank details immediately before payment, linked to the original purchase approval
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action gate scoped to the actual payment payload, tied to the original purchase-approval record, closes the gap created by approving budget before vendor selection, and does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent card with mutual TLS or signed per-request identity
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning/signing the card and replacing the shared static bearer token with mTLS or signed identity prevents impersonation or silent redefinition (rug pull) of the payment peer, independent of model behavior.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7) lets an untrusted vendor-quote email redirect an approved purchase's payment

attack_path.note: Manager approves item and budget before any vendor quote exists.
Untrusted external vendor email supplies the bank details that will actually be paid.
Orchestrator delegates a pay_vendor task containing the quote's bank details to payments-agent over A2A.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no independent destination check; the manager's approval record never reaches it.

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model version/id changes, or observed cases where the agent matches a fraudulent quote to an approved vendor name despite mismatched or altered bank account details.

evidence.observation: Manager approves item and budget before any quote exists; the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no independent verification of the destination.
Orchestrator is instructed to use bank details from the chosen quote and to only pay vendors on the approved list, but the approved-list check is a vendor-name check, not a bank-account verification.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, so the bank details used for payment originate from an untrusted (U) source.

recommendations.action: Bind the payment destination to a verified bank-detail record for the approved vendor (pre-registered/attested account, or out-of-band callback verification), never to the content of an inbound quote email.

Require a fresh, raw-action human approval of the specific vendor and bank details immediately before payment, propagating the original purchase-approval context to payments-agent so the two approvals are cryptographically or record-linked.
Log and alert whenever a payment's bank details differ from the vendor's previously recorded account.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card with static bearer auth enables impersonation or rug-pull of the payment peer

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
Orchestrator will send pay_vendor tasks, including vendor bank details and payment amount, to whatever endpoint/skill the unverified card currently describes.

evidence.observation: Authentication scheme is bearer token only; no mTLS or signed identity declared.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so its declared endpoint/skills can change undetected (rug pull) or be impersonated.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash the payments-agent card/definition and verify it on every fetch; replace the shared static bearer token with mutual TLS or signed per-request identity.

rating.rationale: Two independent paths reach the same irreversible S3 sink (cap.delegate_payment). Finding 1 (authority laundering): the only preventive control on the path is a behavioral, model-dependent prompt instruction that checks vendor name but not bank-account ownership, while the human approval gate occurs before vendor/bank details exist and its context never propagates to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false). That credits one tier of reduction, giving a present-day residual of high, but a model_upgrade trigger defeats the only remaining control and returns the finding to critical. Finding 2 (agent card spoofing/rug-pull): there is no credited control at all today - the card is unsigned and unpinned and authentication is a shared static bearer token - so residual is already critical with no forecast trigger needed. The rollup therefore sets residual and forecast to critical. The single control whose decay most changes the forecast is ctl.vendor_allowlist_instruction, a dependent behavioral check that a stronger model is more likely to satisfy on a fraudulent quote rather than reject.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the payments-agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A traffic logs, DNS, or network configuration were provided for the payments-agent connection; the agent-card spoofing finding (f2) is inferred from documentation alone, so its confidence is medium rather than high.

No runtime/orchestration config was provided for step or time limits; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null and treated as unconstrained per rubric section 4, which is what triggers the autonomy modifier in the inherent risk calculation.

Attack paths are limited to the chain described in the artifacts; no information was provided about further downstream consumers of payments-agent's output or about payments-agent's own internal controls beyond what the runtime notes state.
